name: Long shadow
summary: A shadow far longer than its object, cast by a low sun, so that a still scene feels strange and charged.
how: Cast the shadow at a low angle: the shadow is 2 to 5 times the height of the object.
Keep one light direction in the whole scene.
Leave the shadow flat and dark, at 40% to 70% opacity.
Show the shadow of something outside the frame, to hint at an unseen presence.

origin.note: Giorgio de Chirico paints empty squares with long raking shadows in The Mystery and Melancholy of a Street.

adoptions.via: F. W. Murnau casts the shadow of the vampire on the stairs in Nosferatu.
Surrealist painters take over the empty, shadowed scene of de Chirico.
Flat design adds a 45° long shadow to icons and buttons.
Surreal web scenes use long shadows on calm, empty grounds.

sources.title: Wikipedia, The Mystery and Melancholy of a Street
